A warm container verifies against the OLD public key and rejects tokens signed with the new private key for as long as it lives. THERE IS NO RUNBOOK TO AMEND AND THAT IS STATED RATHER THAN WORKED AROUND: TO-OP-S-10 reads staged and the dual-key overlap runbook is its own deliverable; the project's only rotation runbook is TO-OP-S-3's, for the ORIGIN secret. So the answer is a committed note (e70ca4e244) DELIVERED to TO-OP-S-10's assignee as msg 20226 -- amending a runbook that does not exist would satisfy the criterion's words and none of its purpose. AND A CORRECTION TO THIS FACE'S OWN FRAMING, MEASURED: 'breaks PERMANENTLY, with no mechanism left to repair it' overstates it. The cache is bounded by CONTAINER LIFETIME -- median 5.6 min, p90 52.3, p99 138.0, max observed 143.0 (2.4 h), from 107 measurable spans of 200 streams sampled with NextToken present, so a FLOOR not a census and biased toward recently-active containers. The true shape is a PARTIAL, SILENT, SELF-CLEARING OUTAGE OF UNBOUNDED TAIL DURATION, which is worse than permanent breakage in one respect: permanent breakage gets NOTICED, while a partial outage that clears on its own is absorbed as 'some 401s during the rotation' and never traced to this consumer. THE REFRESH PATH EXISTS AND NEEDS DEPLOYING RATHER THAN DESIGNING: jwtPublicKeys.mjs is two-slot with JWT_KEY_TTL_MS=300000 and accepts both the secret's current bare-PEM shape and its post-rotation envelope. Its own packaging note records that the lib mirror is gated on the consumer having a src/ and that neither portal-authorizer nor auth-validator-edge has one -- session-analytics HAS one, so it is the consumer the shared remedy fits most cleanly. mutant.description: The face names S10C-AC1's instrument test as the control that must be able to fail -- an aliveness oracle that cannot say 'dead' is the one that read ZERO on a function under load. Tested by running the identical query across five functions spanning both outcomes, rather than only against the subject.
mutant.expected: If the instrument were incapable of saying 'dead', every function would return a live-looking number. If it were broken the other way, the known-live subject would read zero.
mutant.observed: Two functions returned metric-absent (auth-validator-edge, deck-generation) and three returned live counts spanning two orders of magnitude -- 141,686 / 4,459 / 2,214. The instrument distinguishes present from absent AND loud from quiet. A SECOND, INDEPENDENT MUTANT sits under S10C-AC2: the build was run twice into separate clean directories, and had the path not been repeatable the two would have differed; had the repo source not been production, both would have differed from the deployed artifact. Neither happened -- 12 of 12 identical in both directions. A THIRD MUTANT CAME FROM ACT TWO and it is the sharpest, because it tests the deploy rather than a reading: the handler moved from index.handler to dist/index.handler, a change that CANNOT fail at deploy time and can only fail at invoke. Had the new path been wrong, the post-deploy invocation would have returned Runtime.ImportModuleError instead of the 401. It returned a response byte-identical to the pre-deploy capture.

determinism.method: The build was executed twice from clean state in separate directories and the outputs compared by sha256; the aliveness query was re-run an hour after the first read.
determinism.observed: Builds: 12 of 12 outputs byte-identical between runs. Aliveness: 141,685 then 141,686 an hour later -- the one-count movement is live traffic, not instability, and a frozen number would have been the suspicious result.
